description: Bringing you the news from a traditional Catholic perspective. title: Tourists destroy statue of Jesus stolen from Divine Mercy church
description: Bringing you the news from a traditional Catholic perspective. ( LifeSiteNews ) — Lithuanian police are still searching for drunk tourists who shattered a golden statue of Jesus from Lithuania’s Shrine of Divine Mercy church, home to the 1934 Divine Mercy painting by Eugeniusz Kazimirowski. … “In the sanctuary of mercy, we repeat every day: ‘Jesus, I trust in You! Today I said these words with pain. I asked the Lord to help me not give in to hate. I prayed that those who have broken His image would understand what they did and know His forgiving love,” continued the priest. “Jesus, I trust in You – even when it hurts, when I don’t understand, when it’s hard to forgive. Jesus, Calm and Humble, with Your help I will surely forgive,” he prayed. Fr. Markauska has appealed for help in locating the perpetrators.

title: Vatican Bank accused of mishandling Archbishop Viganò’s assets
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — LifeSiteNews spoke with Augusto Sinagra, the attorney representing Archbishop Carlo Maria Viganò in a civil case involving the Vatican Bank, to examine allegations that the institution facilitated the unauthorized transfer of the archbishop’s personal fortune and subsequently refused to help recover it. Sinagra is a prominent Italian jurist, professor of European Union law at Sapienza University in Rome, and an attorney admitted to practice before the highest courts. … Sinagra : I have no expertise in canon law, but I observe that, judging by how events have unfolded and continue to unfold, there will be no canonical or other penalties against Polvani or any of the other “ecclesiastical” figures involved in this discreditable affair. LSN : You speak openly of a “Bergoglian vendetta.” Do you believe that the freezing and appropriation of Viganò’s assets were knowingly used by Francis’s curia as a form of financial retaliation intended to suppress the archbishop’s doctrinal denunciations and other criticisms? Would you be able to prove this, or is it merely an assumption you have reached by “connecting the dots” in this affair? Sinagra : Personally, I believe that what Archbishop Viganò has suffered and continues to suffer fits squarely within the framework of a “Bergoglian vendetta,” also in light of Jorge Mario Bergoglio’s overall conduct. I have described Bergoglio as the “Argentine pampero ,” who – significantly – never once paid a visit to Argentina. Obviously, I have no evidence in the technical sense of the term, but one need only apply elementary principles of deductive logic.
